The latest announcement is out from Reliance Worldwide Corp. ( RWC -1.31% ▼ ).

Reliance Worldwide Corporation Limited has dispatched the Scheme Booklet and accompanying shareholder letter for the proposed acquisition of all ordinary shares by an entity affiliated with Brookfield Corporation. The Federal Court of Australia previously approved convening the shareholder meeting and distributing the materials.

The Scheme Meeting will be held on 4 December 2026 in Melbourne, where shareholders will consider the scheme of arrangement. The booklet provides voting and proxy instructions, enabling shareholders to review the proposal and lodge votes before the meeting.

Bloom Energy BE +6.00% ▲ stock is rising in premarket trading on Wednesday after Barclays analyst Christine Cho upgraded her rating from Hold to Buy.She lowered her price target to $289 from $316, which still implies 35% upside from the current level.

The stock also gained after Bloom Energy signed a non-binding agreement with California Resources Corp. CRC -1.60% ▼ to explore fuel cell projects with carbon capture and storage.

Cho noted that Bloom Energy’s customer deposits jumped from $78 million at the end of 2025 to $661 million in Q3 2026. This included a $300 million increase during the quarter. The company’s long-term supply commitments through 2029 also rose to $5.8 billion from $16.4 million in Q2. She said the actual deposits received could be higher because some deposits are counted as revenue once orders are shipped. If customers pay about 10% upfront, the $300 million increase alone could point to at least $3 billion in new contracts.

Cho called this growth “potentially one of the clearest indications yet” that customer commitments to Bloom Energy are picking up.

However, she warned that the company may need to spend more on inventory and production capacity before it earns revenue from those orders. This could keep its 2027 free cash flow below analyst expectations.

Bloom Energy’s Q3 results also showed the impact of higher spending. Revenue jumped 138.1% year-over-year to $1.24 billion, while gross margin reached 34.5%. However, the company reported negative operating cash flow of $27.1 million due to higher spending on working capital.

Under its deal with California Resources, Bloom will provide its fuel cell technology, while CRC will handle CO2 transport and storage.

The projects in Central and Northern California could serve data centers, utilities, and industrial customers. The companies estimate they could capture and store up to 3 million metric tons of CO2 annually. The plans are still subject to final agreements and regulatory approvals.
